resale_co.name: Resale Inspection / Resale Certificate
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Merchantville Code Enforcement (Office of Code Enforcement and Rental Housing Inspection)
requirements: House numbers visible from the street
Fences, decks, sheds and accessory structures must have proper permits
Sidewalks and driveways level and free of trip hazards
Smoke alarm on each level including basement; 10-year sealed lithium battery type
CO detector within 10 feet of sleeping areas (plug-in or battery OK)
2A:10BC fire extinguisher in a cabinet or on a hanger within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)
Handrail on stairs with more than 4 risers; guards on surfaces more than 30 inches above grade
Exterior surfaces painted or protected and in good repair
Yard free of excess weeds, rubbish and garbage
Accessory structures (garages, fences, walls) sound and in good repair
Pools clean; pools over 24 inches deep fenced at least 48 inches with self-closing, self-latching gates

fees.label: Resale re-inspection under Borough Code 25-14 (first re-inspection no charge; this is the second and later)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Resale Inspection Application (includes the smoke detector certificate application) and bring it to the Borough Clerk's office at 1 W. Maple Avenue to pay the fee. Code Enforcement then contacts the applicant to schedule the inspection.

evidence.quote: Before the sale of all residential properties, you are required to obtain a Resale Inspection, including smoke detector compliance. Please bring your completed application to the clerk's office with you to pay the required fee. The Applicant will be contacted to schedule an inspection.
If you have any questions, please contact the Office of Code Enforcement and Rental Housing Inspection at 609-413-0010.
Resale Certificates are only valid for 6 months after passed inspection.
Failure to comply with code requirements may delay or deny issuance of the Certificate of Occupancy and fines issued.
Prior to the resale of all residential and commercial properties within the Borough of Merchantville, a resale certificate from the Code Enforcement Office shall be required.
evidence.doc_date: Code 60B-41, adopted 3-10-2025 by Ord. No. 25-03 (ecode360, legislation through 07-14-2025)

evidence.quote: Residential resale inspection fee$50 per unit ($300 max.)
evidence.doc_date: Code 25-14, amended through 7-14-2025 by Ord. No. 25-08

resale_co.notes: Re-checked October 20, 2026; the Borough page still links 'RESALE PAPERWORK 1-2026' (PDF modified January 21, 2026) with the same fees. New this round: the Borough code was read on ecode360. Code Chapter 60B, Article VI (Resale of Property, Ord. No. 25-03, March 10, 2025) requires a resale certificate from the Code Enforcement Office before the resale of all residential and commercial properties, after a Code Official inspection and a Fire Official check of smoke alarms, CO detectors and fire extinguishers. Code 60B-43 and 25-14 set the resale fee at $50 per unit ($300 max.), matching the form. Reinspection conflict: the form says $10.00, but Code 25-14 says the first reinspection is free and the second and later cost $25; both are listed. The packet asks the intended use of the property, including whether it will be a Community Supervised Living Residence. Rental units need separate registration and a rental inspection/CO before each new tenant (Chapter 60B / rental program), not a resale item. Vacant properties must be registered. Contacts from the page: Code Inspector Tom Connelly, codeenforcement@merchantvillenj.gov, 609-413-0010 (Borough Hall, Tuesday to Friday 8:30 to 4:30); Property Maintenance Officer Kevin Patti, kpatti@merchantvillenj.gov, Niagara Fire Station, 22 East Park Avenue, (856) 488-0404. The resale checklist pages list office phone 856-662-2474.
resale_co.contact_title: Code Inspector (Property Maintenance Officer: Kevin Patti, kpatti@merchantvillenj.gov)

fire_cert.notes: DCA LEA Registry (July 2026) lists Merchantville's Uniform Fire Code enforcing agency as 'F' (Fire Department). The Fire Official (Kevin Patti) is also the Borough's Property Maintenance Officer, working from the Niagara Fire Station at 22 E. Park Ave, and the smoke/CO/extinguisher certificate is applied for with the resale inspection at the Clerk's office. Borough Code 29-8E (amended March 10, 2025) and 25-14 set the same $35 / $70 / $125 tiers and $10 reinspection as the form, so they are not listed twice. These are below the current state amounts ($45 / $90 / $161) but are what the Borough form and code show. The form and code still name a fire extinguisher; the state dropped it from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19), so confirm with the office. The smoke form carries a '09/20' revision mark but is in the January 2026 packet.
